The second caption could move left or sit higher, over the hold planks or the sky, so it clears the rider's chest. It is not a redraw item.

refuted.description: João is not humming, so the caption 'The same hymn the bells had played.' has nothing in the art to refer to. His mouth is shut in a scowl, with no pursed lips, no head tipped to a beat, and no musical notes added at lettering. He also rests an open palm on the sleeper's shoulder rather than cuffing him with the back of his hand, and the tap-one, skip-two count with the strip is not shown.
refuted.reason: I'm refuting this. I zoomed in on page 1, panel 2. João's lips are pressed together and pushed slightly forward, and his head is tipped down and to one side. People hum with their mouths closed, so a shut mouth with the lips pushed out fits the beat. It is not evidence that he isn't humming. The script asks for "lips pursed, head tipped to a beat", and the art shows a close version of that. The drawing doesn't contradict the caption "The same hymn the bells had played.", which picks up the bells from panel 1. His knitted brow suits a jailer humming sourly while he works. The other points don't matter at print size. A palm shoving the sleeper's shoulder wakes the man (his eyes are squeezed shut as he comes to) just as well as a backhanded cuff would, and readers never see the script. A one-tap, two-skip count can't really be shown in a single still panel. He is holding up the notched strip as he works down the line, which is the beat that matters. One optional bit of polish: a small music-note glyph by his mouth would make the hum explicit. That's a nice-to-have, not a major error.

refuted.description: The first sign of the storm is missing. The frame is not canted: the wooden dipper hangs plumb from its peg, and the water in the trough lies level. The hold is warmly lit, not near dark. The script stages the storm only as motion, and this tilt is the baseline that 6.5 must clearly exceed, so the escalation across the page is lost.
refuted.reason: I zoomed panel 6.1 to 3x with a vertical grid laid over it, and the art does not match what the reviewer described. The dipper does not hang plumb. Its handle runs from the peg at the top of the upright down to a bowl that sits clearly left of the peg, about 12 degrees off the panel's vertical border. The upright plank's own edge also leans, by about 8 degrees, so the dipper is visibly off true even against the plank, which is the effect script 6.1 asks for ("hangs off true"). The trough water is not flat either: it carries choppy ripples and a wavy line along the far wall, so it reads as disturbed water. The spill is not strongly lopsided, but that is a small gap at most. On lighting, the panel is dim, with warm lantern glints, much like the rest of the chapter's hold pages (6.2, 6.4). Not hitting "near dark" exactly is a small polish point, not a missing beat. The escalation across the page still works. Panel 6.5 is clearly steeper: the spare chain swings well off true, the frame is strongly canted, there is a shadow at the hatch seam, and a prisoner is praying. So 6.1 reads as the mild first tilt, and 6.5 is clearly beyond it. The story beat is there in the art, and the claim that the dipper hangs "parallel to the panel border" is simply wrong.

minors.description: Nagoji's face drifts from the sheet and from 4.3 right next to it. It is rounder and fleshier, the strong cheekbones are gone, the moustache is thinner and drooping instead of thick and curled, and the hair is shorter, wavier and swept back. He reads as a softer, heavier man.
minors.evidence: Left figure in 4.4, head at about x 665-800, y 880-1060. Compare with Nagoji in 4.3 (x 230-400, y 840-1000) and the nagoji-v2 front and three-quarter heads.

minors.description: Nagoji's face here is broader, older and jowlier than the lean sheet face, with heavy stubble shading on the jaw and chin. Separately, the guard driving the chain is bearded and wears a brown leather jerkin over a cream shirt with a wide belt. That is João's silhouette, doing João's job from 3.3, though João must stay on the wharf. The script asks for a morion and a buff jerkin, which would set him apart.
minors.evidence: Nagoji's head at about x 640-820, y 1540-1640. The guard is at the left, x 108-420, y 1540-1830, with a broad black hat, black beard and brown jerkin.

minors.description: Duarte's hat and satchel don't stay consistent. In 2.3 he wears a weathered, dusty grey-brown slouch hat. In 2.4 it becomes a crisp black flat-brimmed hat, and it is black in 2.2 and 2.5 too. The satchel strap that crosses his shoulder in 2.3 and 2.5 is missing in the 2.4 close-up, though that shoulder is in frame.
minors.evidence: 2.3: hat at about x 300-520, y 1070-1150 is mottled grey-brown, and the strap runs over the viewer-right shoulder. 2.4: the hat at x 860-1165, y 983-1095 is solid black, with no strap on either shoulder. 2.5: the black hat hangs on his back.

minors.description: Nagoji wears gold drop earrings in both ears at once. The bible specifies one small gold ear stud, and the sheet's front view shows a single earring.
minors.evidence: Nagoji's head at about x 340-540, y 1400-1530. Gold drops are visible at both the viewer-left and viewer-right ears (zoom crop of the 6.5 faces).

minors.description: Nagoji's visible ear has no gold ear stud. That is his right ear, which carries the stud on the sheet's front and three-quarter views.
minors.evidence: Nagoji at the lower centre, head at about x 450-700, y 1600-1760. The ear at the viewer's left (about x 540, y 1700) is bare.

minors.description: Lettering hides Nagoji's identity markers in the days-later shot. The caption 'Time on a ship is different from time on land.' runs across his chin and neck. The sailor's balloon covers his body and ochre tunic. Only his eyes, moustache and hair are left to tell him apart from the other curly-haired prisoners.
minors.evidence: Nagoji's head at about x 400-490, y 950-1030. The caption box (x 330-725, y 1022-1085) cuts in just below his moustache. The balloon (x 430-855, y 1125-1250) sits over his seated body.

minors.description: The memory face does not carry Keshavrao's sheet features well. He has a big, voluminous curly mane like Nagoji's and lips tinted bright red, as if wearing lipstick. Next to the short, straight-to-wavy hair on his sheet, he can read as a different youth, or as a younger Nagoji.
minors.evidence: Zoom of the inset face: tight black curls fall to the shoulders, the lips are saturated red, and the moustache is barely visible. Compare 07-keshavrao-v15c.png: coarse straight-to-wavy hair and a natural lip colour.

minors.description: The officer is meant to be seen only in silhouette. Instead he is fully modelled in what reads as a navy-blue coat with a column of gold buttons, a gold-trimmed tricorne, a red cloak and a lace jabot. The look is close to a pirate-captain or Royal Navy officer, and the bible says Portuguese figures must not read as British or Dutch blue-coats.
minors.evidence: Zoom of the officer at top right: brass buttons, a gold-edged hat, a red cape over the shoulder, a white cravat and a brass-hilted sword are all clearly lit. He is not a silhouette.

minors.description: The boarding queue breaks the prisoner palette and the guard lock. Prisoners wear a red tunic, a blue tunic and a mustard-ochre tunic, although the script makes Nagoji's ochre 'the one warm note among grey and brown rags'. Several figures in prisoner rags also wear steel morions. The wharf guard on the right wears a red shoulder cloth and a red waist sash, against the 'nothing red or blue' guard description.
minors.evidence: Zoom of the queue behind the clerk: a blue-tunic figure, a red-tunic figure and a yellow-ochre-tunic figure stand in line. The two leftmost queue figures wear morion and kettle helmets with ragged tunics. In the zoom of the guard on the right, red cloth shows at the shoulder and the waist.

minors.description: The guard driving the chain wears a red waist cloth under his belt, against the guard lock (buff jerkin, no red or blue).
minors.evidence: At left foreground, a red sash shows at the waist beneath the buff jerkin and sword belt.

minors.description: Nagoji's bandaging changes between consecutive panels on the same page. In 6.4 his bandage wraps the whole hand and runs up the forearm to the elbow. In 6.5, the next moment, only a short band is wrapped at the wrist, and the hand and forearm are bare.
minors.evidence: 6.4: a heavy linen wrap from the knuckles to the top of the frame on the arm entering from the left. 6.5: a single narrow wrap above the manacle on the screen-left forearm, with bare skin above it and a bare hand.

minors.description: In 4.2 Nagoji's index and middle fingertips are bandaged, as the script asks. In the very next panel, 4.3, and everywhere else in the chapter, his fingers are bare. The forearm bandages also vary from page to page: short wrist bands in 1.3, wraps from wrist to elbow in 4.3 and 4.4.
minors.evidence: 4.2: two fingertips wrapped in linen. 4.3: both hands below the manacles have bare fingers. 1.3: narrow bands at the wrists only.

minors.description: The collar chain setup breaks from the surrounding two-shots. In 4.3, 4.4, 5.1, 6.1 and 6.5, one slack chain links Nagoji's and Keshavrao's collars. In 5.3 each man has his own chain hanging straight down from the front of his collar, and a third chain hangs from a post ring between them, linked to neither.
minors.evidence: 5.3: vertical chains drop from both collar fronts to below the frame. The post-ring chain between the two heads is separate.

minors.description: Nagoji's collar ring is drawn at the front, under his chin, but the bible's chapter 2 row specifies 'a hinged iron collar with a ring at the side'. Other panels (2.3, 2.5, 5.5) put it at the side, so the collar is inconsistent across the chapter. 4.3 and 6.5 also show the ring at the front.
minors.evidence: 1.3 zoom: a hasp and ring hang at the centre of his throat. 1.4: a ring at the front of the collar. 2.5: the chain attaches at the side of the collar, behind his jaw.

minors.description: Nagoji drifts off-model in 4.4. The face is rounder and softer and the hair thinner and less curly, unlike the angular face in 4.3 directly beside it. Half his head is also cut off by the left frame edge.
minors.evidence: Zoom of 4.4: a broad, rounded jaw, smaller eyes and a sparse wavy fringe. In 4.3 the same character has high cheekbones and a full curly mane, as on nagoji-v2.png.

minors.description: Duarte's leather satchel strap, prominent over his left shoulder in 2.3 and again in 2.5, is missing from the tight shot in 2.4, where that shoulder is fully in frame.
minors.evidence: 2.3: a wide brown leather strap runs across the screen-right shoulder to the bag at his hip. 2.4: the screen-right shoulder and chest are plain black cassock with no strap.

minors.description: The wrist irons on the climbing prisoners do not match the 'short slack chain' lock. Their arms swing wide at their sides, and the wrist chain runs behind the back, so it must be far longer than a forearm.
minors.evidence: Zoom of 2.1: the lead man's wrists are wider apart than his shoulders, with a chain stub trailing behind him. The second man's chain loops behind his back between cuffs hanging at his sides.

minors.description: The reading order is unclear. The first caption, "They woke us under cover of bells.", sits in the top-right corner, and the second, "I counted the strokes.", sits to its left and slightly lower, so a left-to-right reader can hit "I counted the strokes" first, which makes no sense before the bells. The path then zigzags back right to João's balloon. João's balloon also sits over the shoulders and torso of the foreground Nagoji.
minors.evidence: "They woke us" box is at about (1186-1626, 361-451) px. "I counted the strokes" box is at about (569-866, 452-535) px. The "Up! Those marked go to the docks." balloon is at about (1025-1495, 570-695) px, covering the body of the figure at the right edge.

minors.description: João's balloon is a tall, narrow pill holding five lines of two or three words each. Its tail ends at his belt and chest rather than heading toward his mouth, and the bottom of the balloon almost touches the panel's bottom border.
minors.evidence: The "On your feet, marata. The Viceroy has found a use for you." balloon is at display (328-520, 1070-1300). Its tail tip is at about display (420, 1000) at João's waist, while his mouth is at about (420, 905). The balloon's bottom edge is within a few pixels of the panel border at y 1308.

minors.description: The caption box crowds João's face: its left edge butts against his cheek and ear. The top of his head is also cut off by the panel's top border.
minors.evidence: "The same hymn the bells had played." box starts at display x 593, directly against João's head (about x 480-595, y 530-600). His crown is cropped at the top border, y 530.

minors.description: The lettering style does not match the approved Chapter 1. Ch1 sets caption text left-aligned and uses thin-outline elliptical balloons with left-aligned text. Ch2 centres all caption text and uses heavy-outline rounded-rectangle balloons. Side by side in one book, the two chapters look lettered by different hands.
minors.evidence: Ch1 r6 page 9 "They are gathering us for transport." (oval, thin rule, left-aligned) and "Ships meant movement." (caption left-aligned), and Ch1 page 2 "Este. This one is stubborn." Compare Ch2 page 1 "Up! Those marked go to the docks." (rounded rectangle, heavy rule, centred) and "He knew where I sat..." (centred caption). The same Ch2 style is used on pages 1 to 6.

minors.description: The top-left caption is set with almost no inner padding: the first line runs from edge to edge of the box, and the last line is a one-word widow. Other captions on the page have generous margins. Panel 2.1 has the same widow pattern ("stone.").
minors.evidence: In "I filed his face away in the part of my mind that kept / accounts.", the "I" sits about 15 px from the box's left rule and "kept" about 28 px from the right rule. In 2.1, "The climb was like being born through a tunnel of / stone." leaves "stone." alone on line 2.

minors.description: The tail of "To Angola. Africa." stops in open sky among the masts and reaches no figure. "Not this one. The Jesuits need bodies..." sits on Nagoji's chest directly under his face, so at a glance it can read as his line, although its short tail points left to the old prisoner.
minors.evidence: "To Angola" tail tip is at about display (195, 800), roughly 70 px above the turbaned prisoner's head at about (155, 870). The "Not this one" balloon is at display (350-785, 818-938), immediately below Nagoji's face at about (470, 700-800). Its tail exits left at about (325, 885).

minors.description: The Portuguese guard driving the chain is cropped at eye level by the panel's top border, so his face is lost on a full-width panel that has room above.
minors.evidence: The guard's hat and eyes are cut by the top border at display y 1537, at about x 300-390. Only his nose, beard and mouth remain.

minors.description: The off-panel sailor's tail rises from the balloon directly past Keshavrao's head to the grating, so the line can be misread as his. The "Time on a ship..." caption also covers Nagoji's torso in the pen, which the script asks to be seen in the middle distance.
minors.evidence: The "Wind is with us..." tail runs from about display (800, 1125) to (815, 935), passing within about 15 to 20 px of Keshavrao's face at about (760, 1050). The caption at display (328-725, 1022-1085) sits over Nagoji's body below his face at about (440, 990).

minors.description: Some balloons are set as tall, narrow columns pressed against the panel edge, with two or three words per line, which breaks the reading rhythm compared with the wider balloons elsewhere.
minors.evidence: In 5.3, "We are not there yet. As long as we move, there is a chance." runs to six lines at display (288-478, 688-915) against the left border. In 5.5, "God sends opportunity. These bodies are silver if they live." runs to five lines at display (1015-1213, 1262-1490) against the right border.

minors.description: The caption covers Keshavrao's forearm where it joins the hand closed over Nagoji's bandaged wrist. In this hands-only panel, his hand therefore reads as disembodied, which weakens the clasp that is the panel's whole action.
minors.evidence: "Neither of us mentioned that promises made in chains are the easiest to break." box is at display (803-1215, 1095-1188). Keshavrao's fingers are at about (640-800, 1120-1190), and his forearm continues right behind the box.

minors.description: João leans back away from the gangplank and hauls the taut chain toward himself, in a tug-of-war with the ship's hand at the top. This reads as holding the prisoners back while he shouts 'Faster.' His balloon also covers most of the climbing prisoners on the plank.
minors.evidence: Page 3, third strip: João's weight is on his back foot at left with both fists pulling the chain toward himself. The chain runs taut up-right to the line on the plank, and the balloon hides everything on the plank except feet and Nagoji's head.

minors.description: Nagoji is drawn as a large close-up, taking up the left half of the harbour panel, where the script wants his chain small in the foreground under the looming ship. He wears a confident half-smile while the old prisoner says they will be worked until they forget their names. His ochre is not 'the one warm note': prisoners in the line behind wear red, orange and blue.
minors.evidence: Page 3, large second panel: Nagoji's head and shoulders fill the left-centre above the balloons, chin lifted with a slight smile. In the queue behind the clerk, several prisoners wear red, orange and blue cloth.

minors.description: João does not have his back to the tally scratches. The scratches are in plain view on the wall between him and Nagoji, so 'He knew where I sat' loses its point that the gaoler stands over the marks without seeing them. Nagoji also looks up and away to the right, not at João, who stands on the left addressing him.
minors.evidence: Page 1, panel 3: vertical tally strokes are visible on the stone just right of João's shoulder, beneath the caption. Nagoji's face is tilted up toward the upper right while João stands at left.

minors.description: The 'slow, painful rise' reads as calm. Nagoji's face is composed, with no wince behind a set jaw, and both hands are braced on the wall rather than one.
minors.evidence: Page 1, panel 4: Nagoji crouches with both bandaged hands flat on the wall and a relaxed, almost serene expression.

minors.description: 'Rao.' is lettered as a normal solid speech balloon. The script marks it as a whisper (NAGOJI (whisper)), and with a guard walking the line it should read as one.
minors.evidence: Page 1, bottom strip: 'Rao.' sits in a standard solid-outline round balloon with a full tail to Nagoji's mouth, the same style as João's shouted lines.

minors.description: Duarte's hat and satchel change between adjacent panels. In 2.3 he wears a weathered grey-brown broad hat with the satchel strap over his shoulder. In 2.4, the next panel, the hat is crisp black and the satchel strap is gone.
minors.evidence: Page 2, middle-left panel: worn, mottled grey-brown hat and leather strap across the chest. Middle-right panel: smooth black hat, and no strap on either shoulder.

minors.description: The men at the hatch are not silhouetted. Both sailors are fully lit and grinning, and the officer's coat details (gold buttons, red lining, lace jabot) are clearly visible. Sailor 2, who says 'This run is cursed. They say God sends warnings.', is smiling broadly, which undercuts the superstitious line the officer answers.
minors.evidence: Page 5, bottom panel: the head-cloth sailor under the 'This run is cursed' balloon tail is grinning in full sunlight. The officer at right shows his buttons and red lining, with only his face in shadow.

minors.description: The days-later wide is mostly covered by lettering. The caption hides Nagoji's body and the sailor balloon hides Keshavrao's lower half. The sailor's long tail rises right beside Keshavrao's face, which risks attributing the line to him. The panel is also indented rather than full width as scripted, and the light is warm orange rather than dim grey through the grating.
minors.evidence: Page 5, fourth strip: 'Time on a ship...' covers Nagoji below the chin. The 'Wind is with us...' balloon's tail starts at Keshavrao's shoulder and runs up to the grating. The strip's left and right edges sit inside the full-width strips above and below.

minors.description: The courtyard is ordinary bright daylight, not 'burned almost to white so the glare hurts'. The shock of the light after the cellar is weaker than scripted.
minors.evidence: Page 2, second strip: a clear pale-blue sky, fully modelled musketeers and walls, and normal contrast across the frame.

minors.description: On the stair the prisoners' wrist cuffs are not joined by the short chain that 1.5 and the Chapter 2 continuity row require; each man's hands hang apart. The climb is also an open curved stair with a church and palms in plain view at the top, so 'a tunnel of stone' going from black to white is only partly shown.
minors.evidence: Page 2, top strip: every climber wears separate iron cuffs on each wrist with no chain between them, and arms swing apart. The right side is an open parapet, and a whitewashed church sits fully visible at upper right.

minors.description: João's balloon covers almost all of Nagoji in the foreground. Only his upturned profile and one bandaged wrist show, so the establishing 'only Nagoji wears ochre' figure in three-quarter back view is lost.
minors.evidence: Page 1, top strip: the 'Up! Those marked go to the docks.' balloon sits over the lower right, hiding Nagoji's torso and tunic. Only his head, moustache and ear stud show above it.
